# Genesis Apocryphon Column 22 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** 1QapGen (Cave 1), Col. 22 | **Condition:** Well preserved; substantially legible

---

**22:1** He also assigned Hagar to Sarai as her personal servant.

**22:2** The king lavished gifts upon me — silver, gold, and fine clothing,

**22:3** linen and purple cloth — placing them all before me.

**22:4** And Hagar too he gave to Sarai as a handmaid.

**22:5** So I, Abram, departed a wealthy man, with enormous flocks, silver, and gold.

**22:6** I left Egypt, taking with me my entire household.

**22:7** Lot came along with me. He too had grown wealthy, with large herds of livestock,

**22:8** and had married a woman from among the Egyptian women.

**22:9** I camped [...] at each of my previous stopping places until I arrived at Bethel,

**22:10** the very place where I had first built an altar.

**22:11** I rebuilt the altar and offered burnt offerings and a grain offering upon it

**22:12** to God Most High. There I called on the name of the LORD

**22:13** and gave praise to God, saying: You, O God Most High, are my God forever and ever!

**22:14** From there I traveled [...] southward [...] until I reached Hebron.

**22:15** Hebron was already built by that time. I settled there for two years.

**22:16** Then a famine struck the whole land, and I heard there was grain to be had

**22:17** in Egypt. So I prepared to travel to Egypt [...]

**22:18** I reached the Karmon River, one of the tributaries of the Nile,

**22:19** [...] and I crossed [...] the seven branches of this river [...]

**22:20** I passed through our land, crossing the breadth of [...]

**22:21** and crossed into Egypt.

**22:22** Then God said to me: Look out from the place where you stand —

**22:23** to the north and to the south, to the east and to the west.

**22:24** All the land that you can see, I am giving to you

**22:25** and to your descendants forever.

**22:26** I will make your descendants as countless as the dust of the earth — if anyone could count

**22:27** every grain of dust, only then could your descendants be counted.

**22:28** Get up! Walk the length and breadth of the land,

**22:29** for I am giving it to you. So I, Abram, set out on a journey to explore

**22:30** and see the land. Starting from the Gihon River,

**22:31** I followed the coast until I reached the Taurus Mountains.

**22:32** From [...] the Great Salt Sea I went along the Taurus range

**22:33** eastward across the breadth of the land until I reached the Euphrates River.

**22:34** I followed the Euphrates until I came to the Red Sea in the east.

---

*PNEUMA notes: Column 22 is well preserved and brings the Abraham cycle to its grand geographic conclusion. The departure from Egypt (22:1-8) establishes Abraham as a man transformed — wealthy, blessed, and accompanied by Hagar (the future mother of Ishmael). Lot's Egyptian wife is a striking detail unique to this text. The divine land-promise (22:22-29) repeats Gen 13:14-17 with the powerful dust metaphor. The final geographical survey (22:30-34) traces the boundaries of the promised land in a grand circuit.*
